The columns that contributed most to this risk are age, education, industry, marital_status, and sex. Each of these columns decreases the risk. This means that the information in these columns makes it harder to link this record to a specific person. For example, if many people share the same age or education level, it protects their privacy.

To improve privacy, we could better anonymize the columns. For example, we could group ages into ranges instead of using exact numbers. We could also use broader categories for education and industry. This would make it even harder to connect the record to someone specific. 

Risk scores represent ML model confidence under simulated attack conditions, not real-world re-identification probability.
